tests.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2
tests.creator: Artificial Analysis
tests.measures: One synthetic score that averages ten independent tests of agents, coding, scientific reasoning and general knowledge.
tests.items: 10 evaluations (AA-Briefcase, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience, HLE, GDP.pdf, CritPt)
tests.format: Composite index (weighted average: Agents 30%, Coding 20%, Scientific reasoning 20%, General 30%)
tests.saturation: Not saturated: top model 57.6 (Claude Opus 5.5, max effort) on 2026-10-06, unchanged on 2026-10-08.
tests.known_issues: Version changes often (v4.0 Jan 2026 to v4.3.2 Sep-Oct 2026); scores are not comparable across versions. Each reasoning-effort setting is scored separately. English, mostly text.

tests.name: Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI)
tests.creator: Epoch AI
tests.measures: One capability score fitted across dozens of benchmarks, so that models tested on different benchmarks can be compared on one scale.
tests.format: Statistical composite (item-response-style fit over many benchmarks)
tests.saturation: Not saturated (open scale).
tests.known_issues: Depends on which benchmarks each model has results for; very new models (e.g. Gemini 4 Argon, MiMo-V2.6-Pro, Mistral Large 4) not yet scored.

tests.name: LMArena Text Arena (overall)
tests.creator: LMArena
tests.measures: Which answer people prefer in blind side-by-side chats, turned into a rating.
tests.saturation: Not saturated, but the top 20 models sit within about 40 points with overlapping confidence intervals.
tests.known_issues: Measures preference, not correctness; sensitive to style and length (style control applied by default); new models have few votes and wide intervals (marked preliminary). The site now redirects from lmarena.ai to arena.ai ('formerly known as LMArena'); no new snapshot after 2026-10-02 as of 2026-10-08.

tests.name: GPQA Diamond
tests.creator: David Rein, Samuel R. Bowman et al. (GPQA paper)
tests.measures: Very hard graduate-level multiple-choice questions in biology, physics and chemistry that cannot be answered by simple web search.
tests.human_baseline: PhD-level experts 65% (74% discounting clear mistakes); skilled non-experts with web access 34% (on the full GPQA set, per the paper abstract).
tests.saturation: Near saturation: best scores around 95-96% (Epoch AI, Artificial Analysis). Removed from the AA Intelligence Index in v4.2.
tests.known_issues: Small set (198 questions), so differences of 1-2 points are noise; the paper notes that experts reach 74% once clear mistakes they identified are discounted, so a few answers are disputable and the practical ceiling is below 100%.

tests.name: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE)
tests.creator: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI
tests.measures: Expert-written closed-ended questions across dozens of academic subjects, designed to be the hardest academic exam for AI.
tests.format: Exact-match short answers and multiple choice (24% MC, 14% need an image)
tests.saturation: Not saturated: about 61% without tools (Claude Opus 5.5, AA); vendors report up to 67.7% with tools.
tests.known_issues: With-tools and no-tools scores are mixed in announcements; answer grading uses an LLM judge (judge choice differs between AA, Scale and vendors); CAIS released an updated "HLE-Rolling" set on 2026-09-17.

tests.name: FrontierMath Tiers 1-3 (v2, private)
tests.creator: Epoch AI
tests.measures: Unpublished research-level mathematics problems with automatically checkable answers.
tests.saturation: Approaching saturation for the very top (93.7% for GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol).
tests.known_issues: Held privately and run only by Epoch AI, so results cannot be reproduced by third parties.

tests.name: FrontierMath Tier 4 (v2, private)
tests.creator: Epoch AI
tests.measures: The hardest tier of FrontierMath (research-level problems).
tests.saturation: Saturating at the very top (GPT-6.1 Sol 100%, GPT-6 Astra 97.6%, Claude Opus 5.5 95%) but wide spread below.
tests.known_issues: Very small number of problems, so each problem moves the score by several points.

tests.name: OTIS Mock AIME 2024-2025
tests.creator: Epoch AI (problems from the OTIS mock AIME)
tests.measures: Competition mathematics at the level of the American Invitational Mathematics Examination, on problems less likely to be in training data than the official AIME.
tests.saturation: Saturated: several models at 100%.
tests.known_issues: Used here as the AIME proxy because Artificial Analysis retired AIME 2025 and no independent AIME 2026 table covering current models was found.

tests.name: ARC-AGI-2
tests.creator: ARC Prize Foundation
tests.measures: Visual grid puzzles that are easy for humans but require learning a new rule from a few examples.
tests.human_baseline: Human panel 100% (ARC Prize data, about $17 per task).
tests.saturation: Near saturation at the top (GPT-6 Astra 95%).
tests.known_issues: Scores depend on reasoning effort and cost; ARC Prize reports cost per task alongside score.

tests.name: ARC-AGI-3
tests.creator: ARC Prize Foundation
tests.measures: Interactive game environments where an agent must discover the goal and the rules by playing, scored on how efficiently it learns compared with humans.
tests.unit: % score (100% = beats every game as efficiently as humans)
tests.saturation: Far from saturated with the standard harness (best 62.7%, GPT-6 Astra max effort).
tests.known_issues: ARC Prize also publishes a "Provider Adapter" harness where some models score near 100%; the two harnesses must not be mixed.

tests.name: SWE-bench Verified
tests.creator: SWE-bench (swebench.com), human-verified subset
tests.measures: Fixing real GitHub issues from open-source repositories, checked by running unit tests against the generated patch.
tests.saturation: Saturated: 97.0% (Claude Opus 5, Vals.ai, mini-SWE-agent). Vals.ai no longer runs it on new releases and vendors stopped reporting it.
tests.known_issues: Strong contamination risk (public repositories); scores vary a lot with the agent harness; newest models (Sept 2026) not tested.

tests.name: SWE-Bench Pro (public set)
tests.creator: Scale AI
tests.measures: Harder, contamination-resistant software engineering tasks from copyleft and private codebases.
tests.items: 1,865 tasks in total; public set 731, private set 276, held-out 858
tests.saturation: Not saturated, but the public SEAL leaderboard has not added models released after mid-2026 (latest entry Muse Spark 1.1).
tests.known_issues: Most current frontier models have no SEAL result; vendors use their own harnesses.

tests.name: Terminal-Bench 4.0
tests.creator: Stanford University researchers, Laude Institute and open-source community
tests.measures: Completing hard multi-step tasks in a command-line terminal (software, system administration, data, ML, security).
tests.format: Agentic terminal tasks, each graded by its own test suite
tests.saturation: Not saturated (best 63.6% independent, 70.6% vendor-reported).
tests.known_issues: Harness matters: AA uses mini-swe-agent (3 repeats), vendors use their own (Claude Code etc.); version 4.0 replaced 2.0/2.1 in 2026, so older Terminal-Bench numbers are not comparable.

tests.name: τ³-Banking (tau-bench family)
tests.creator: Sierra
tests.measures: A customer-support agent that must search a large knowledge base and make correct account changes while talking with a simulated user.
tests.saturation: Not saturated (best about 51%).
tests.known_issues: Replaces τ²-Bench Telecom in AA reporting (τ²-Bench Telecom saturated above 95% for many models); removed from the AA Intelligence Index in v4.3 but still run as a standalone evaluation; not run for every new model.

tests.name: OSWorld 2.0 (binary completion)
tests.creator: XLANG Lab (osworld-v2.xlang.ai)
tests.measures: Long, realistic computer-use workflows on a real desktop (about 1.6 hours median for a human).
tests.format: Agentic computer use (GUI and tools), 500-step budget
tests.human_baseline: Median human operation time about 1.6 hours per task (no human success rate published).
tests.saturation: Far from saturated (best 31.4% binary on release v2026.08.08).
tests.known_issues: Several releases (v2026.06.24, v2026.08.08, v2.1) with different scores; vendors report OSWorld 2.1 or subsets with partial scores; very few models on the public board.

tests.name: OSWorld 2.0 / 2.1 (partial score)
tests.creator: XLANG Lab (osworld-v2.xlang.ai)
tests.measures: Same tasks as OSWorld 2.0, with partial credit for sub-steps completed.
tests.saturation: Not saturated.
tests.known_issues: Mixes independent (2.0 leaderboard) and vendor-reported (2.1, offline subset) values: compare only within the same version and source.

tests.name: METR 50% task-completion time horizon
tests.creator: METR
tests.measures: The length of software, ML and cybersecurity tasks (in human-expert time) that an AI agent completes with 50% probability.
tests.items: Over a hundred tasks (RE-Bench, HCAST and shorter tasks), Time Horizon 1.1 suite
tests.format: Agentic tasks; logistic fit of success vs. human task duration
tests.human_baseline: Task lengths are calibrated on skilled professionals (about 5 years of experience on average).
tests.saturation: Suite near its limit: METR states measurements above 16 hours are unreliable.
tests.known_issues: No measurement published for any model released after April 2026 (last update 2026-05-08, Claude Mythos Preview at about 1,045 min); very wide confidence intervals.

tests.name: MMLU-Pro
tests.creator: TIGER-Lab
tests.measures: Broad academic knowledge and reasoning in 14 subjects, harder than the original MMLU.
tests.saturation: Saturated: Vals.ai no longer runs it on new releases; top 92.4% (Claude Fable 5.1). Removed from the AA index in v4.0.
tests.known_issues: No independent results for models released after early September 2026.

tests.name: LiveCodeBench
tests.creator: LiveCodeBench team (livecodebench.github.io)
tests.measures: Competitive programming problems collected continuously from LeetCode, AtCoder and Codeforces to limit contamination.
tests.format: Code generation checked by hidden tests
tests.saturation: Saturated on easy and medium splits; Vals.ai no longer runs it on new releases; top 90.5%.
tests.known_issues: Results depend on problem date window and version; removed from the AA index in v4.0.

tests.name: SimpleQA Verified
tests.measures: Short factual questions that test whether a model knows facts without inventing answers.
tests.format: Short open answers graded for correctness
tests.saturation: Not saturated (best 75.6%, GPT-6 Astra).
tests.known_issues: Measures parametric knowledge without web search; models that abstain more score lower on accuracy but hallucinate less.

tests.name: AA-Omniscience
tests.creator: Artificial Analysis
tests.measures: Knowledge across six domains, rewarding correct answers and penalising confident wrong answers (hallucinations).
tests.saturation: Not saturated (best 46.4).
tests.known_issues: A negative score means the model gives more wrong answers than right ones instead of abstaining; part of the AA Intelligence Index.

tests.name: APEX-Agents
tests.creator: Mercor
tests.measures: Professional-services tasks completed by an agent working with files and tools, graded by rubric.
tests.saturation: Not saturated (best 82.2%, Gemini 4 Argon).
tests.known_issues: Run by the benchmark owner; values here are compiled by Epoch AI; standard errors of about 4-5 points.

caveats: Reasoning effort matters: most 2026 models expose several effort levels (low to max). Epoch AI and ARC Prize values here are the best setting reported; Artificial Analysis values use the highest-effort configuration listed (named in each note). Cost changes a lot between settings (ARC-AGI-2 cost per task for Claude Opus 5.5: $0.24 at low effort vs $1.85 at max).

Harness matters for agentic tests (Terminal-Bench, SWE-bench, OSWorld, ARC-AGI-3): e.g. Gemini 3.1 Pro on Terminal-Bench 2.0 scores 80.2% with TongAgents vs 59.4% with Gemini CLI (tbench.ai via Epoch AI), and GPT-6 Astra scores 62.7% on ARC-AGI-3 with the standard harness vs 98.6% with the Provider Adapter. Only compare values from the same source.
Versions change: Terminal-Bench 2.x vs 4.0, OSWorld 1.0 vs 2.0 vs 2.1, AA Intelligence Index v4.0 to v4.3.2, HLE vs HLE-Rolling. Never compare numbers across versions.

Vendor-reported values (kind = "vendor") are run by the model maker with its own settings, often with tools and maximum effort; seven such cells are included (all OSWorld partial scores) and many more vendor figures are kept in notes. Independent values are preferred throughout.
HLE: the independent AA values are without tools; vendors mostly publish with-tools values (4-7 points higher in Anthropic's own no-tools vs with-tools figures).
Saturated tests (GPQA Diamond, OTIS Mock AIME, SWE-bench Verified, MMLU-Pro, LiveCodeBench, ARC-AGI-2 at the top) no longer separate frontier models; gaps of 1-2 points are within noise.
LMArena measures human preference (style, tone) rather than correctness; new models with few votes are marked preliminary and their rank can move.

Composite indices (AA Intelligence Index, Epoch ECI) depend on their component choice and weights; they rank the same top models differently in places (e.g. Claude Sonnet 5.5 is 2nd on AA, 4th on ECI).
Open-weight status follows Artificial Analysis and LMArena licences; Epoch AI classifies GLM-5.3 as closed weights, which conflicts.
Grok 4.7 creator appears as "SpaceXAI" on Artificial Analysis and LMArena and as xAI on Epoch AI and ARC Prize.

Dates: "date" is the publication or run date of the measurement where available (Epoch run start date, LMArena snapshot 2026-10-02, Vals.ai 2026-09-01); otherwise the date of first retrieval (2026-10-06, or 2026-10-08 for values added on that day). Every value was re-read at its source on 2026-10-08 and none had changed; dates were kept.

Gemini 3.1 Pro (Preview), Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 29.72 (v4.3.2): confirmed on 2026-10-06 as the only configuration listed. Its knowledge scores match Gemini 3.8 Flash (HLE 47.0% vs 47.8%); the gap comes from the agentic tests (Terminal-Bench 4.0: 4.0% vs 19.7%; GDPval normalized 0.147 vs 0.468), read from the data embedded in https://artificialanalysis.ai/leaderboards/models.

Claude Haiku 5.5 counts more tokens than Haiku 4.5 for the same text (newer tokenizer, about +30% per Anthropic), so per-token prices and per-task costs are not directly comparable across the two generations.
Artificial Analysis lists Mistral Large 4 Preview at its list price ($1.36/$4.18) and a 524,288-token context, whereas Mistral's own page shows the launch price ($0.68/$2.09) and 1M tokens.
